answer: An agent registry named lantern can require each identity vertex to submit a proof of replication for a 10 GiB dataset encoded with its public key, then answer unpredictable storage audits. To forge extra identities, an attacker must maintain additional encoded replicas or pay to recompute them before audit deadlines. This imposes storage or computation cost per identity; specialized hardware and cheap disks can still make large Sybil fleets affordable.
